sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

content.text:
Case F39: segment the fibrous soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 241x241x216 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

content.thinking: I'll begin by looking at seg_open.

content.text:
case F39 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(241, 241, 216) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: fibrous soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 108/216 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: There's a large mass in the thigh region - I should look through the axial sequence of the segmentation sheet to assess it further.

content.thinking: The tumor spans roughly axial slices 40 to 170, appearing as a large heterogeneous mass in the thigh, with a dark round structure likely representing the femur shaft near the center-left. I want to check the coronal and sagittal views to better define its full extent.

content.text: sheet coronal 60–180/241 (12 slices) | v0 | tool calls 3/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: This tumor spans a large coronal range, roughly slices 60 to 160. I'll begin with a point prompt on the largest axial slice, checking slice 107 or 92 first.

content.text: axial 107/216 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 4/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: The tumor dominates much of the thigh, and the dark circular structure near center-right looks like the femur, with a dark cortical ring surrounding the marrow. I'm thinking of placing a positive point marker in the center of the tumor region to guide segmentation.

content.text: version v1 (parent v0) | volume 125.8 mL | components 138 (largest 97.7%; 137 others total 2.8 mL) | extent axial 61–171, coronal 50–150, sagittal 44–128 | change +125.8 mL / 0.0 mL | tool calls 5/40, prompts 1/15 | point add (1 mark(s)) | image: axial 93, coronal 96, sagittal 86 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking:
The segmented mask at 125.8 mL only captures part of the heterogeneous tumor, missing the intermediate-signal region on the right side of axial 93 -- the actual mass appears to occupy most of the thigh, likely with hypointense fibrous components creating signal heterogeneity that the model under-segmented.

I'm examining axial 107, where the entire region from the dark femur to the outer muscle boundary looks tumorous, including that lateral rim of intermediate signal. Rather than more individual prompts, I'm weighing a broader approach -- a lasso around the outer boundary on this slice, or painting a rough outline followed by refinement -- while tracing the tumor's actual spatial extent relative to the surrounding thigh musculature.

I think the lasso approach makes the most sense given the heterogeneous intensity, since it captures everything inside the boundary regardless of texture variation. Let me view axial 107 with edge marks overlaid so I can trace the true tumor boundary before drawing the lasso.

content.text: axial 107/216 | crop full | marks edges | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 6/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
The mask placement seems to differ from what I saw on the earlier slice. Looking at the clean image, the tumor seems to occupy the deep thigh compartment roughly from x≈230-640, y≈280-610, though the lateral region at x 540-640 looks more homogeneous and the boundary between tumor and muscle isn't clearly distinguishable.

Given this looks like a heterogeneous fibrous soft tissue tumor, I'm leaning toward treating the entire bulky region bounded by the fascia as tumor. I'll trace a polygon around the full outer boundary on axial 107 using the available edge marks to define the lasso.

The left-side "tail" extending toward the hamstring region looks like a separate thin structure that might be a tumor extension along the fascia rather than normal muscle, and I notice similar bright tissue on that tail in axial 154, which complicates the outline. Given this complexity, I think it's better to place a few more point prompts spread across the tumor and let the model's intensity-based segmentation refine the boundary rather than trying to trace every edge manually.

Though I'm also considering drawing a full lasso polygon around the whole mass in axial 107 — including the grayer lateral part that the point prompts might miss — ordering the boundary points clockwise from the top and working around through the lateral, inferior, and medial edges toward where the mass meets the femur and posterior muscles.

The femur itself sits center-left as a dark circle, with the tumor wrapping around it; since cortical bone is dark, excluding it from the polygon boundary shouldn't matter much since the model likely wouldn't pick it up anyway. I'm leaning toward simplifying the lasso to trace the mass contour while roughly skirting the femur edge, rather than trying to carve out its exact boundary.

I'll go with the lasso approach on the current axial slice using the edge markers visible in this view, tracing a polygon from the upper markers down around the right side and back along the left, accepting that it may clip slightly into the femur's edge since the model should still exclude dark bone regardless.

I'm uncertain whether the mid-gray tail extending toward the lower-left is tumor or muscle/tendon—leaning toward excluding it for now since it doesn't clearly match the tumor's signal pattern.

I'll call seg_lasso with the positive polygon I've traced.

content.text: version v2 (parent v1) | volume 605.9 mL | components 13 (largest 99.9%; 12 others total 0.2 mL) | extent axial 31–195, coronal 49–157, sagittal 41–135 | change +480.1 mL / -0.1 mL | tool calls 7/40, prompts 2/15 | lasso add | image: axial 111, coronal 97, sagittal 89 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking:
The mask now measures 606 mL and covers the full mass outline across these planes—axial 111 follows the outer tumor boundary while excluding the femur and tail, coronal 97 covers the mass well, and sagittal 89 appears to include the whole mass with a plausible anterior boundary. I'm noting that in axial 111 the outline on the left side runs along the femur edge.

Looking more closely at the posterior region in axial 111, it seems to be tumor rather than muscle. I'm weighing whether the gray lateral region is actually normal vastus lateralis muscle or lower-signal fibrous tumor tissue—since fibrous tumors can show intermediate-to-low T2 signal while brighter areas suggest myxoid or necrotic components, so including that gray periphery as tumor seems correct. I want to cross-check this against other slices like axial 76 and 138 to confirm the boundary.

I'll pull up a few slices with overlay outlines—axial 76, 138, 154, 60—and specifically check axial 150 to verify the lower part and that gray lateral region.

content.text: axial 140/216 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 8/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
Looking at axial 140, I'm checking whether the mask boundary aligns with the mass versus an adjacent structure—there's a separate rounded, intermediate-gray region with a bright rim nearby that could be a muscle like vastus intermedius rather than tumor, and the mask seems to exclude part of its upper-left portion.

The overall mask forms a broad outline with a few negligible small fragments (about 0.2 mL total), not worth trimming given the main mass is already 99.9% of the volume. I want to verify the superior and inferior boundaries more carefully, checking slices around axial 76, 61, and 160, and confirming the full craniocaudal extent runs roughly from axial 31 to 195.

content.text: axial 180/216 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 9/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
At axial 180, there's a crescent-shaped bright structure around the posterior-lateral femur — I'm wondering if this represents femoral vessels/muscle or possibly tumor extension wrapping around the bone at this distal thigh level.

It's hard to tell from the earlier axial 185 whether this is a neurovascular bundle or tumor periphery. Since the mask's distal extent is uncertain, I want to check the coronal and sagittal views for the tumor's inferior boundary — coronal spans roughly 49–157, sagittal 41–135, and axial 31–195, so the distal slices (160–195) likely contain only thin, ambiguous structures that I should verify with an overlay at axial 160.

content.text: axial 160/216 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
At axial 160, the mask aligns with the gray tumor mass, bounded by fascia with a smooth lateral edge — that checks out. At 180, there's a brighter crescent that could be a distal tumor extension near the femur, though it's small; I'll keep it in since the mask spans 31–195.

That raises the question of what's happening at the top around axial 31 — maybe a small leak above where the mass actually starts, since earlier views showed the mass beginning around axial 45 with just vessels visible lower at axial 30. I should check axial 40 with the overlay to see what's really there at the top.

content.text: axial 45/216 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 11/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
I'm examining the axial slice near the hip/proximal femur, noting that the mask only partially covers the bright lobulated region — likely tumor tissue sitting posterior-medial to the femur, with the dark circular structure nearby probably representing the ischium or femoral head.

I should check a coronal or sagittal view to understand the proximal extent better, maybe looking at coronal slice 97 near the superior edge of the mass. I'm thinking I could add a positive point on the bright region in axial 45, but I need marker IDs from the current view first, so I'll pull up seg_view with coarse marks on axial 45 to get those coordinates.

content.text: axial 50/216 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 12/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
I'm trying to identify the anatomy at axial slice 50 — the bright oval could be a vessel, and the darker circle might be part of the hip joint or proximal femur, but it's ambiguous at this level. The mask region at this slice only covers a thin area.

Looking at the propagated mask across slices 31-195, the proximal levels are only partially covered — the posterior gray-bright area is mostly included but the left portion isn't captured. Given the time budget is fine so far, I'm planning to add another positive point prompt to extend coverage at the proximal slice.

Checking the past-the-mask panels for residual lesion tissue, I notice most show nothing, but coronal slice 41 at 8mm posterior to the mask has a bright blob that looks like it could be part of a tail structure rather than actual lesion.

I'm trying to reconcile left/right orientation—the mask's coronal indexing is confusing since "posterior to mask" at index 41 seems to be labeled oddly relative to the mask extent. The bright blob at coronal 41 is probably a femoral vessel rather than tumor tissue, matching the very bright oval seen on axial 50 that looked more like fluid or a vein than tumor. The coronal 129 panel just confirms the mask's anterior-left extension, nothing new there.

None of the candidates is accepted since they are muscle/fascia shell or small outside tissue. Uncertainty remains at the proximal tip near the bright oval structure and the anterior-medial margin.

content.text: case F39 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v3 | final volume 681.9 mL, components 2 (largest 99.9%; 1 other totals 0.0 mL) | tool calls 19/40, prompts 3/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

The segmentation for F39 is saved as version v3: 681.9 mL across two connected components, with the largest holding 99.9% of the volume. Confidence is medium.

- **Method:** I placed one positive point in the bright centre of the mass, then drew a lasso around the whole outer boundary on axial 107, which captured the gray lateral part that the point alone missed. A second positive point pair on axial 50 extended the proximal posterior part.
- **Checks:** The outline follows the outer tumour edge on axial, coronal and sagittal views. It excludes the femur and the thin tail structure on the lateral side. The past-the-mask panels in the final review showed no clear extra lesion.
- **Candidates:** I rejected all five automatic proposals. C1 to C3 are muscle and fascia shell outside the mass, and C4 and C5 are small anterior or superior bits of normal tissue.
- **Remaining uncertainty:** The proximal tip is less certain, since the mask stops at the edge of a bright oval structure near axial 50 that I treated as a vessel. The anterior-medial margin around axial 140 is also only partly covered. The distal crescent around the femur near axial 180 is small and included, and may be normal tissue.
